items.title: From Kala Pani To A New Prison Policy: Andaman-Nicobar To Scrap 130-Year-Old Prisons Act
points: India's prison system is set for a significant legislative change in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, with the introduction of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Prisons and Correctional Services Regulation, 2026.

The new rule under Article 240 of the Constitution will replace three colonial-era and older laws applicable to the Union Territory: The Prisons Act, 1894, the Prisoners Act, 1900, and the Transfer of Prisoners Act, 1950.

The move marks a shift in how prisons are administered, moving beyond an approach centred largely on custody, punishment and control to one that places greater emphasis on rehabilitation, healthcare, education and preparing inmates for life after release.
The change carries particular significance for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, home to the Cellular Jail, popularly known as Kala Pani.
The historic prison was once used by the British to incarcerate and punish freedom fighters during India's struggle for Independence.

Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the duty hike effected from May has "slowed down" gold imports "a bit" so far this year, from around USD 60 billion every year.

In May, the government had hiked import duty on gold and silver to 15 per cent, from 6 per cent, to contain non-essential imports.

items.title: Gadkari Says He's Responsible For 40% Of India's Air Pollution: What He Actually Means
points: Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has made a striking admission about the pollution caused by India's growing vehicle population.

An October 2026 assessment by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air drew attention to studies that identified industry, household emissions and power generation as major contributors to fine-particle pollution.
One of the studies placed transport's share of secondary PM2.5 exposure at 11%.
That is a different measure from overall air pollution, so it cannot simply be used to disprove Gadkari's 40% claim.

According to the Coast Guard, the icebreaker logged more than 17,000 nautical miles during the voyage and was the only U.S. surface vessel working in the High Arctic.
Under Operation Frontier Sentinel, the ship monitored foreign-flagged research vessels for over 300 hours across the Arctic.
No polar icebreaker had carried out a designated law enforcement mission in more than 20 years before the Storis patrol.
On July 21, Operation Tundra Merlin placed the icebreaker in the Arctic waters alongside Coast Guard cutters Munro and Fir and the Royal Canadian Navy ship HMCS Max Bernays.

'Five defining features': Jaishankar decodes the changing world order
points: During his speech in Japan, S Jaishankar highlighted concerns about the weaponization of the global economy, noting key trends that are redefining international relationships such as strategic rivalry and resource manipulation.
He stressed the necessity for trustworthy alliances and diversification amid economic uncertainties.
Jaishankar further advocated for deepened collaboration between India and Japan across multiple sectors, as this could foster enhanced stability in the Indo-Pacific region.
